description: Tithi start and end instants - the sharpest test of Moon-Sun elongation, and the quantity most sensitive to delta-T at historical dates.

source.notes: UNPOPULATED. REQUIRED. State whether the printed tithi is the UDAYA tithi (the one running at sunrise, which is what a patro row usually names) or the tithi at some other instant, and which ayanamsha. The udaya-vs-instant distinction changes which tithi a day is labelled with, so a mismatch here is a convention difference, not an engine error. Do not fill from this engine's own output — the loader rejects a self-referential authority.

tolerance.rationale: Tithi boundaries are printed to the minute in almanacs, and the elongation rate near a boundary means a small longitude difference becomes a larger time difference. 180 s reflects that amplification; see docs/timescale-contract.md section 3 for why BCE entries would need far wider tolerance.

todo: PRIORITY 2 — gates Phase 7. Needs tithi end instants for one lunar month from an authoritative Nepali patro, modern dates only. Include at least one kshaya (skipped) tithi and one adhika (repeated) tithi if the month has them — those are exactly where the udaya rule bites and where an extraction is most likely to change an answer. Do NOT add BCE entries: at 3000 BCE a tithi end time carries roughly +/- 2 h from delta-T uncertainty alone (docs/timescale-contract.md section 3), so a tight golden value there would be false precision.

entry_shape.date: YYYY-MM-DD civil date the patro prints this row against
